programmes.d: In Mexico, Josh is hired to protect a man and his pregnant wife from his the villagers who are angered when he refuses the town healing woman or "witch" from being present when his wife gives birth.
After Josh takes the task of finding a man and his wife's pet ewe, he becomes the butt of many jokes while cattlemen nearly hang him when he mentions sheep. His only clue is a gold bell the ewe wore.
When a convicted killer escapes prison, Josh is hired to protect the woman whose testimony put him there. The woman's husband is a lawyer who says he has always been a coward and never carries a gun.
Josh rides into a town looking for a man who wants to hire him. When he goes to the man's room at the hotel, Josh is shot. He must figure out who shot him but the sheriff is ordering him out of town.
Josh is hired by Harry Weaver to track down his twin brother Pete, a wanted man. Harry is tired of being used by Pete, plus the law and bounty hunters are apt to mistake him for Pete.

Josh is called in to track down a new outlaw, the local sheriff who is a friend. The good sheriff who was seduced into robbing a bank by his girlfriend, convinces Josh to let him assist in her capture
Josh takes a job protecting a deaf teenage girl and keeping everyone off the father's place for a day or two. Although initially bored, Josh starts to develop a relationship with the friendly girl.
Josh escorts a photographer to take a picture of his friend El Gato, who is a hilarious bandit living in the hills of Mexico with a small army. However, El Gato is new to photographs and leery.
A broke Josh is hired by a fearful man to help him elope with his sweetheart, Jane, the daughter of a local rancher. The girl's father is vehemently opposed to the marriage.

Josh takes a job protecting an express office employee who stole $10,000 and wants to return it before it's discovered missing. However, he had an accomplice and does not know where the accomplice is.
A Japanese woman travels to the U.S. to find a man who proposed to her and hires Josh to find him since no one will help her. Josh is confronted by the Japanese man to whom she had been promised.
Josh arrives in town thinking the sheriff summoned him to go after a man. Instead, a woman wants Josh to bring in the man, her wanted husband, alive, so he can prove self defense.
Josh rides to Barney Durant's horse business right after Barney pushes his son to leave. When Josh's prisoners escape taking 2 horses from his horse trader friend, he helps in tracking them down.
While pursuing Carl Martin, Josh stops at a marshal's office and is falsely accused of the marshal's murder.
When phony wanted posters seek a retired Confederate officer, Colonel Sykes' daughter summons Josh to help.
An old man with an Apache bodyguard is wanted for a crime committed long ago.
A ranch manager hires Randall to bring back a line rider charged with grand theft.
Randall is rooked into advancing half the bounty to a man who promises to lead him to Shawnee Bill.
A banker hires Randall to track down the man he believes responsible for his son's death and a bank robbery.
Randall must transport a killer to Tucson, but exchanges him for the nun kidnapped by the killer's gang.
The townspeople of Pot Hole are in the grip of a bully who serves as the hanging judge over a kangaroo court
Josh escorts a beautiful woman to trial, and she uses all her charm on him to convince him she is innocent
Josh is asked by Stacy Torrance for help when she finds a wanted poster for her for murder.
Josh agrees to go to the lawless town of Bent Horn to bring back a man wanted for bank robbery and murder.
Josh sets out to help a wife locate her missing husband, but his mission meets with a resistant townspeople.
Josh is bushwhacked by bounty hunters who must keep Josh from reporting their illegal "bounty game".
A sadistic pair of killers escape from prison. They hijack the stagecoach Josh is riding with a young prisoner
Randall and a gentleman unaccustomed to the West must trek to safety across many miles of Apache territory.
Randall receives his most daunting assignment yet from a boy who has eight cents to pay: bring in Santa Claus.
Thieves are waiting to ambush mail carriers and Josh is hired to help insure that the mail will get through.
Josh is knocked out by a posse who wants his prisoner.
Josh needs to get his wounded prisoner to Bannach in three days to prevent an innocent man from hanging.
Josh rides into a small town looking for Vic Warsaw but is told that Warsaw was killed the night before.
4 men break out of prison looking for revenge against Aben Starr who turned them in.
Josh is resting when two bounty hunters bring in a dead man. The sheriff wants nothing to do with the pair.
A grieving father who is the town drunk hires Josh Randall with his last $30 to find his murdered son's body.
At the request of his friend's wife, Randall comes to protect a war buddy in his bid for the town's mayoralty.
Josh honors a dying friend's request to return his body to Cameron and the townspeople believe Josh killed him
Josh is approached by the wife of a man eager to turn himself in, provided Josh split the bounty with his wife
A man with unwavering faith in a legend about lost treasure hires Josh to lead his family on an expedition.
When a runaway is framed for killing a Pinkerton agent, Randall turns detective to uncover the real killer.
Josh is requested to meet a famous singer in Denver who has a job for him.
Josh comes to the aid of an old friend who is being strong-armed into selling the Outrider Hotel and Saloon.
Josh goes into the Apache camp to win the hand of a woman the Indians kidnapped as a child.
Pursuing killer Joe Collins, Josh is followed by a man who believes Collins could be his lost son.
A religious cult cast lots and it falls upon a young woman to act as its angel of vengeance.
A young orphan girl wants Josh to find the parents she insists are still alive.
A father hires Josh to retrieve his son, an ideologue being used by plunderers to recruit freedom fighters.
Josh's browbeating about ending a decades-long feud gets him drafted to reconcile the hate-fueled hillbillies.
